item.title: Casual Ride (D) - GS Pretzel Logic (22F) RSVP Required — Sun Aug 2, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup Ride leader: Jan Zerfoss Anticipated Average Pace for D rides: (12-14 mph) Route: [GS Pretzel Logic (22F)](https://routes.lancasterbikeclub.net/cue/gs-pretzel-logic-ride-22f/) **Be Safe, Have Fun, and Ride Together**
This is a Casual D Class ride. The ride leader will ride at the advertised average speed. This is intended to be a group ride with a no-drop rule as the main goal. The ride leader will do his/her best to keep the group together with occasional regroupings and/or splitting into multiple groups to align to pace capabilities.

item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Aug 2, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Aug 4, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description:

Lancaster Freethought Society is a community for Freethinkers, Atheists, Agnostics, Humanists, Non-believers, Skeptics, and those who are simply curious. There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. item.description:
Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors
Best for adults and older interested teens. Registration is appreciated but not required if space allows.American Disasters is a six-session PowerPoint series. Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.
